title: Split network infra modules to enable regional outputs and cross-account compatibility
creator: Sofia Ramirez
body: Context: Our monolithic networking Terraform module has grown large and inflexible for multi-region and cross-account deployments. This causes long plan/apply times, brittle state operations, and blocks Dedicated/private customers who need region-scoped outputs and simpler cross-account role assumptions. Goal: Break the single networking module into smaller, composable region-scoped modules (vpc-core, vpc-subnets, vpc-peering, vpc-outputs) and provide a compatibility wrapper so existing stacks keep working while we migrate. Scope: - Extract region-aware outputs so downstream stacks can reference region-specific subnet IDs, AZ mappings, and NAT/IGW resources without graphing the entire global state. - Add cross-account role outputs and explicit assume-role module to support Dedicated/private on-prem peering patterns. - Upgrade AWS provider to >= 5.9 and pin to 5.x bracket to avoid breaking changes; update required_providers blocks. - Introduce a migration plan with terraform state mv scripts and idempotent apply paths. - Add automated tests in infra-ci: parallel terratest runs per-region and a state-migration dry-run job. Design decisions and trade-offs: - We intentionally duplicate some resource modules (small surface area) to keep module boundaries clear; this increases repo files but reduces plan scope and reduces locking contention. - We will maintain a thin root compatibility module that calls the new regional modules so most existing stacks only need minor variable updates. - Provider upgrade to 5.x is risky for some legacy resources; the plan includes a gated roll-forward per environment and provider-pin in modules to limit blast radius. Acceptance criteria: - New modules live under infra/modules/network/{vpc-core,vpc-subnets,vpc-peering,vpc-outputs}. - CI runs terratest suites for us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and passes in the integration stage. - Migration scripts (state move + mapping docs) are added to infra/ops/migrations/network-refactor. - No disruption to prod stacks: run staged migration in non-prod, then prod after sign-off. - PRs merged with at least two infra reviewers and one security reviewer. Migration/rollout plan (high level): 1) Merge modules behind feature flag and land compatibility wrapper PR. 2) Run terratest + state-migration dry-run in staging. 3) Execute state mv scripts for each workspace with small window; monitor infra-console and SLO dashboards. 4) Roll forward provider upgrade once state is stable. 5) Deprecate legacy module after all workspaces have migrated (announce and set a 60-day sunset). Risks and mitigations: - Terraform state mv mistakes: mitigation = automated dry-run, peer review of mapping, and snapshot backups to S3 with KMS. - Provider upgrade breaking resources: mitigation = provider pinning and a canary workspace for a single non-prod region. - Increased cognitive load for new contributors: mitigation = clear README per module, example usages, and workspace templates. Testing strategy: - Unit: terraform validate and fmt in pre-commit. - Integration: terratest infra-ci jobs per region. - Smoke: deploy a small tenant stack via the compatibility wrapper. Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/3456789/Regional+Networking+Refactor GitHub PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2145 State migration script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/ops/migrations/network-refactor/state-moves.sh
comments: 2026-02-20: Triage completed. Decided to split modules rather than incremental refactor to get faster plan times.
2026-02-24: Pairing session with networking team — agreed on module boundaries and outputs. Action: Kai to draft compatibility wrapper.
2026-02-28: Provider upgrade impact assessment added to Confluence. Identified ~4 legacy resources needing explicit attribute changes.
2026-03-04: First terratest run failed in eu-west-1 due to subnet tagging mismatch; fixed mapping in vpc-subnets module and re-ran.
2026-03-09: Security reviewed cross-account assume-role pattern; requested MFA optionality and additional audit logging on role creation.
2026-03-12: Initial PR opened #2145, awaiting infra reviewers. Next: run staged state-migration dry-run in staging workspace.
